purpose: Bootstrap record of the desktop runtime transport configuration and the upstream support wording, cited as evidence by the capability register entry desktop.runtime-transport.stdio. It is evidence only and grants no eligibility.

runtime.framing: newline-delimited JSON, no jsonrpc field, 64 MiB line limit
runtime.stderr: captured separately to a bounded buffer and a log file; never parsed as protocol

transports.notes: Only transport the desktop requests. The runtime is an owned child process; the main process is its only client.

upstreamWording.section: Connect a remote Code Mode host
upstreamWording.context: Remote Code Mode host. The warning is stated in this context and must keep it.
upstreamWording.quote: The app-server command and WebSocket transport are experimental and aren’t supported for production workloads.

upstreamWording.summary: Lists JSONL over stdio as the default transport and separately marks the TCP WebSocket transport experimental and unsupported.

upstreamWording.quote: [experimental] Run the app server or related tooling.

upstreamWording.quote: [experimental] Generate TypeScript bindings for the app server protocol.

upstreamWording.context: App-server daemon used by remote-management clients; not used by the desktop.
upstreamWording.quote: `codex-app-server-daemon` is experimental and its lifecycle contract may change while the remote-management flow is still being developed.

interpretation: Default stdio availability establishes neither blanket production support nor Inquello readiness. The selected fork and route must be verified and hardened before release.
productionEligibilityReason: Upstream labels the app-server command experimental, and the capability register (Story 1.9) holds this transport at synthetic-only, and no Inquello hardening or release verification exists yet.
